_about: Esto no es lo que pedí: dinner at La Cocina de Lucía. Two set-ups: Lucía at the host stand (3 pictures: the welcome, the wait twist, inside or the terrace) and Luis at the learner's table (11 pictures: drinks?, the aguas frescas, the order, the cochinita served, the wrong-dish twist, the cold-soup twist, taking a dish back, dessert, the check, the card terminal and the tip, goodbye). 14 pictures for the longest conversation of the chapter (five twists). The window-table and factura twists change nothing seen: they keep the seat and check pictures.

s73-restaurant.npc: Lucía, restaurant host (host stand) · Luis, waiter (table)

items.prompt: Lucía, the owner and host of La Cocina de Lucía, stands behind the dark wooden host stand near the entrance, about one third from the left, one hand resting on the stack of menus with blank covers, the other open in welcome. A warm, generous smile ("¡Buenas noches! ¿Tiene reservación?"). Warm evening light; a few diners far in the soft background.
Change only her pose: she glances back over her shoulder at the full dining room, then turns to the learner with an apologetic smile, one hand raised palm out (a short wait for a table).
Change only her pose: she holds two menus with blank covers against her chest and sweeps her other open hand toward the dining room and the terrace, a welcoming smile (inside or on the terrace?).

Luis, the waiter, stands beside the learner's table in the dining room of La Cocina de Lucía, about one third from the left, a small blank notepad in one hand and a pen in the other, leaning in slightly with an obliging smile ("¿Qué les traigo de tomar?"). Seen from the learner's seat: the near edge of a wooden table with an embroidered cotton runner, an open menu with blank pages, a folded napkin and cutlery; the host stand far behind in the soft background.
Change only his pose: he sets a tall glass of deep-red agua de jamaica on the table in front of the learner with one hand, a clay pitcher of milky-white horchata in his other hand, a friendly smile.
Change only his pose: he writes on the blank notepad with the pen, eyes on the learner, nodding attentively (taking the order); the menu lies closed on the table.

Change only his pose: he sets down a plate of cochinita pibil (shredded orange-red pork with bright pink pickled onions, black beans and rice) and a small basket of tortillas wrapped in an embroidered cloth in front of the learner, a proud smile ("¡Buen provecho!").
Change only his pose: he sets down in front of the learner a plate with a whole grilled fish in red achiote paste on a banana leaf (tikin xic), smiling confidently, unaware it is the wrong dish.

Change only his pose: a bowl of sopa de lima (clear broth with shredded chicken, crisp tortilla strips and a slice of lime) sits in front of the learner, with no steam rising from it; he leans in with his hands behind his back, eyebrows raised ("¿Qué tal la sopa?").
Change only his pose: he lifts a dish back off the table with both hands, shoulders raised in apology, an embarrassed, sincere look ("¡Perdón! Ahorita se lo cambio.").
Change only his pose: he holds a small plate of flan with glossy caramel sauce at chest height, presenting it with a tempting smile ("¿Algo de postre?"); the table is cleared.
Change only his pose: he places a small closed dark-leather check folder (blank) on the cleared table in front of the learner with one hand, a courteous smile.
Change only his pose: he holds the card terminal out toward the learner with both hands, its screen blank, waiting politely with a small smile (the tip, usually 10 to 15 percent).
Change only his pose: he stands upright by the cleared table, one hand on his chest, giving a small courteous nod goodbye, a warm smile ("¡Gracias por su visita!").
